name: Islamic tile mosaic
summary: Wall and dome cladding that the Seljuk and Timurid potters made from glazed tiles in one colour. They cut each tile into small shapes and set the pieces together in a geometric or calligraphic pattern.

philosophy.core_thesis: A building surface becomes a woven pattern of light and colour when many small tiles in turquoise, cobalt and black are cut to fit one geometric plan.
design_principles: Glaze each plain tile in one colour: turquoise from copper, blue from cobalt, black from manganese and iron.
Cut the fired tile with a chisel into the shapes of one pattern: stars, kites, lozenges and calligraphic strokes.
Draw the full pattern first, then set the cut pieces face down on it and pour plaster over the back.
Build the pattern on a grid of 6, 8 or 12 points so that the shapes repeat without a gap.
Use the Kufic script as a band 30 to 60 cm wide, in white or blue on a dark field.
Keep the tesserae 1 to 2 cm thick, with joints under 2 mm, so that the surface reads as one skin.
Place the mosaic on the parts that people look at: the mihrab, the portal and the dome.
Add a few lustre or relief tiles to a flat mosaic for a change of light.
anti_patterns: A painted pattern on a flat tile, with no cut joints
Figures of people and animals in the mosaic field
Thick grout lines that break the pattern into squares
Bright modern colours such as pink, lime green or orange
A single repeating tile that makes a wallpaper pattern with no cut shapes

form.shape: Cut-tile panels for domes, portals, mihrab niches and walls, tile friezes with Kufic script, and small star-and-cross wall tiles with lustre.
form.profile: A flat face with a very small relief: the cut pieces lie in one plane, and relief bands and lustre tiles add a slight change.
form.foot_and_rim: Panels have no foot. The edge of a panel meets a plaster or brick frame, and a border band of two or three lines closes the pattern.
form.proportion: Tesserae are 1 to 6 cm across and 1 to 2 cm thick; star-and-cross lustre tiles are about 20 cm square.
rules: Cut every piece to the pattern; do not paint the shapes on a large tile.
Keep the colours to five: turquoise, cobalt, black, white and a little lustre.
Close each pattern with a border band that keeps the grid of the field.

bodies.rule: Use a white stonepaste of quartz, glass frit and a little clay for the tile. Use a red earthenware for the plain backing. Keep porcelain and stoneware out: they do not suit this glaze.

methods: pressing the tile in a flat mould
drying the tile in the shade
chiselling the fired tile into small shapes
setting the pieces face down on a drawn pattern
forming.joins: The pieces are bedded in plaster over a brick or rubble wall, and the joints are filled with a thin mortar.
forming.details: Chisel marks on the back of each piece, a sharp cut edge on the glazed face, and a slight change of level between neighbours.

glaze.pattern: Interlocking stars, kites and girih shapes in turquoise, cobalt and black, with white Kufic inscriptions and a little lustre on small wall tiles.
glaze.gloss: Bright and glassy, about 70 to 90 GU, with a slight iridescence where the glaze is old.
glaze.wear: Alkaline glaze gives a silver bloom and fine crazing after centuries; some pieces fall out and leave a pale plaster ground.

palette.strategy: A turquoise and cobalt field with black lines and white script; lustre and gold give a warm accent.

firing.kiln: A small updraught kiln fired with wood or brushwood; the tiles stand on stilts in saggars.
processes: biscuit firing of the pressed tile
glaze firing of each colour in its own batch
a third, reduction firing at about 600 °C for lustre tiles
cold cutting of the fired tile
firing.scale: One dome needed tens of thousands of cut pieces; workshops in Konya, Kashan and Samarkand worked for one patron at a time.
firing.signs: Small kiln stilt marks on the back of the tile, a copper-green edge on some turquoise, and irregular colour from batch to batch.

pieces.form: Dome panel of cut turquoise, cobalt and black tiles in stars and kites
Mihrab niche with a Kufic inscription in a frame of cut tiles
Square tile of 20 cm with a lustre star and a cross pattern
Frieze band with a white Kufic inscription in raised letters on a blue ground

positive: turquoise cobalt and black glazed tiles

canonical_works.work: Dome and mihrab of the Karatay Madrasa, Konya
Tile mosaic of the Sırçalı Madrasa, Konya

evidence.title: Karatay Madrasa, Konya, tile mosaic dome

emotion.target_response: A calm, deep awe: the viewer sees a wall of small bright pieces that form one endless pattern and reads it as order and prayer.

use_cases: a mosque or madrasa portal in tile
a geometric tile pattern brief with a closed colour set
a museum label on medieval Islamic tile work
avoid_when: the brief needs a painted figure scene
the brief wants a pale modern colour set
the brief is for a hand-made flat floor tile

modifiers.how: Change the body to terracotta with a tin glaze, and chisel the tiles into small pieces for a pattern with an 8-point star.
Change to a painted tile with a white slip and a clear glaze, and paint tulips and carnations in cobalt, turquoise and red.

wall_thickness.note: Cut tesserae are 8 to 20 mm thick; a lustre wall tile is about 12 mm.
